                                     INTRODUCTION

Q. Please state your name and address.​

A. My name is Ryan Hopkins. My business address is 2923 CR 202, Burnet, TX 78611.

Q. Can you remind the Judges of your business?​

A. Yes, I own and operate my business, Lone Star Land Protection (LSLP). LSLP

provides landowner-side consulting for Texans affected by energy, utility, mineral, and

infrastructure projects.

Q. Have you been tendered as an expert witness in this matter?​

A. Yes, I was tendered as an expert witness by G6 Landowners Legal Fund, LLC, and

no party filed objections to my testifying as an expert witness.

             PURPOSE AND BASIS OF CROSS-REBUTTAL TESTIMONY

Q. What are the purposes of your cross-rebuttal testimony in this proceeding?​

A. Parties in this proceeding filed direct testimony through which witnesses proposed

alternative routes that included the G6 link. I have reviewed and analyzed that testimony

and the exhibits or attachments used to support that testimony. The purpose of my

cross-rebuttal testimony is to provide the Administrative Law Judges and the Public

Utility Commission of Texas ("Commission") the results of my analysis considering the

statutory and regulatory factors that the Commission is required to consider under

PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B); and applying those factors specifically




                                                         Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Ryan Hopkins​
                                        on Behalf of the G6 Landowners Legal Fund LLC regarding ​
                                                 Reinecke Testimony for Cherokee Creek Partners
                                                                            PUC Docket No. 59475​
                                                                 SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                      Page 4 of 29
 to the alternative routes that included the G6 link that were proposed in direct testimony

on behalf of other parties in this proceeding.

Q. Were your cross-rebuttal testimony and related attachments prepared by you

or under your supervision?

A. Yes.

Q. Are your cross-rebuttal testimony and related attachments true and correct to

the best of your knowledge and belief?

A. Yes.

Q. What is the basis for your cross-rebuttal testimony in this proceeding?​

A. My testimony is based on my expert opinions, which are within my areas of

expertise: transmission line right-of-way acquisition, transmission line siting, parcel-level

constraints analysis, and the statutory and regulatory framework that governs CCN

proceedings for high-voltage transmission lines under PURA § 37.056 and 16 TAC §

25.101. In addition, for this cross-rebuttal I have conducted an independent multi-route

composite scoring analysis of 123 routes, the 122 routes filed with the Application and

the additional route proposed by Ms. Reinecke on behalf of Cherokee Creek Partners

(“CCP”), using data sourced entirely from the Applicants' own filed materials. That

analysis is described in detail in the Affirmative Route Analysis section of this testimony.

 Q. What materials have you reviewed in the preparation of your cross-rebuttal for

this proceeding?​

A. I have reviewed:

      (1) the Application filed by Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA

Transmission Service Corporation in this docket, including the route-tier shape files and

constraint disclosures for the G6 Link;

      (2) the direct testimony of Rae Lynn Schneider Reinecke - President/Owner,

Integrated Environmental Solutions, LLC (IES), McKinney, TX on behalf of Cherokee

Creek Partners; Bonnie Helene McAnelly (individually and as Trustee of the 2025

Homestead Trust and the Bonnie Helene McAnelly 2023 Trust (collectively referred

herein as “CCP”) (Interchange Filing No. 4204);

      (3) the direct testimony of Aaron Brewer, P.G., Managing Director, Natural

Resources, ESE Partners (Austin, TX) (Interchange Filing No. 4494) and Barry T.

Smitherman on behalf of Save The Lampasas, Carpenter Land & Cattle, Martin, and the

N3 Opposition Landowner Group (collectively referred herein as “STL”)(Interchange

Filing No. 4339); and

      (4) Applicants’ Response to CCP’s Request for Information regarding alternative

routes requested by CCP, including Route CCG (Interchange Filing No. 3787).

I have reviewed and analyzed the testimony and the exhibits or attachments used to

support that testimony and applied the statutory and regulatory factors that the

 Commission is required to consider under PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 TAC §

25.101(b)(3)(B) to prepare the opinions I present in this cross-rebuttal testimony. I have

also conducted an independent composite scoring analysis of 123 routes using the

Applicants' own filed data, as described in detail below.

                                SUMMARY OF OPINIONS

Q. Based upon your understanding of the Application; your education,

experience, and expertise; and your review of the testimony you have just listed

and the exhibits or attachments used to support that testimony, have you formed

opinions as to issues relevant to the criteria required for Commission approval in

PURA § 37.056(c)(4); 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B)?

A. Yes, I have.

Q. In your expert opinion, did you identify flaws or omissions in the analysis

provided by Ms. Reinecke in her direct testimony that are relevant to the criteria

required for Commission approval in PURA § 37.056(c)(4); 16 TAC §

25.101(b)(3)(B)?

A. Yes, I did, as follows and as discussed in further detail below:

       (1) Ms. Reinecke advocates for the substitution of G6 for G51-G52 and N4 for N3

but does not analyze these substitutions at the individual-link level;




                                                         Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Ryan Hopkins​
                                        on Behalf of the G6 Landowners Legal Fund LLC regarding ​
                                                 Reinecke Testimony for Cherokee Creek Partners
                                                                            PUC Docket No. 59475​
                                                                 SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                      Page 7 of 29
       (2) Commission rules require consideration of engineering constraints and cost,

but Ms. Reinecke fails to perform an engineering or cost analysis of CCP’s proposed

routes;

      (3) Ms. Reinecke’s proposed route, Route CCG, has approximately 41 more

structure-type identifications than Route 894, but Ms. Reinecke inappropriately deems

the presence of this greater number of structures immaterial;

      (4) Ms. Reinecke’s reliance on USFS Landscape Aesthetics Handbook viewshed

methodology and the Bureau of Land Management (“BLM”) Visual Resources Inventory

(“VRI”) Manual is inconsistent with Commission rules and prior Commission orders; and

      (5) Ms. Reinecke’s Table RLSR-16 regarding volume of protests by link

contradicts her G6 recommendation. G6 and other links in CCG were in the top 20 for

most protest forms/opposition letters, including C4 (222 mentions, most opposed), D12

(105, 6th), C5 (95, 7th), and G73 (59, 9th), all part of CCG's eastern link sequence. Her

recommendation of Route CCG is not supported by her analysis.

Q. Have you conducted an affirmative analysis to identify which routes best meet

the statutory criteria?

A. Yes. Because multiple witnesses filed direct testimony recommending G6-based

routes, specifically Route 572 (Brewer), Routes 295 and 296 (Brewer alternatives), and

Route CCG (Reinecke), I conducted an independent composite scoring analysis of all

123 routes (122 application routes plus the 1 CCP-suggested route - Route CCG) to

                                                                                     Page 8 of 29
 identify which routes affirmatively best meet the statutory and regulatory criteria of

PURA §37.056(c)(4) and 16 TAC §25.101(b)(3)(B). The model I present here

incorporates an expanded and more granular weighting structure, built category by

category from the statute itself and the public record in this proceeding. The result was,

to me, genuinely surprising: when the statutory weights are applied correctly and

transparently, the Applicants' own proposed route, Route 894, emerged as the

top-ranked route of all 123 routes.

                 CROSS-REBUTTAL OF REINECKE TESTIMONY FOR CCP

Q. Did you review the direct testimony of Rae Lynn Schneider Reinecke -

President/Owner, Integrated Environmental Solutions, LLC (IES), McKinney, TX on

behalf of Cherokee Creek Partners; Bonnie Helene McAnelly (individually and as

Trustee of the 2025 Homestead Trust and the Bonnie Helene McAnelly 2023

Trust?

A. Yes, I did.

Q. For the record, how is Ms. Reinecke’s testimony designated in the PUC

Interchange filing system?

A. It was filed as PUC Interchange Item No. 4204.

Q. Did Ms. Reinecke’s testimony include Exhibits to support her testimony?

A. Yes, her testimony included 18 Exhibits and is comprised of approximately 450

pages.
                                                         Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Ryan Hopkins​
                                        on Behalf of the G6 Landowners Legal Fund LLC regarding ​
                                                 Reinecke Testimony for Cherokee Creek Partners
                                                                            PUC Docket No. 59475​
                                                                 SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349

 Q. Did you review those Exhibits as part of your review and analysis of her

testimony?

A. Yes, I did.

Q. Based on your review of Ms. Reinecke’s testimony and Exhibits, how would

you summarize the objective of her testimony?

A. Ms. Reinecke's testimony is a 91-page narrative focused on one move - she replaces

nineteen Route 894 links (G51, G52, H1, H41, H42, J21, J22, J23, J27, J4, K11, K7,

J16, K13, K51, K52, M11, M12, N3, I11) with a different sequence built around G2-G6

and M5-N4, and asks the Commission to designate the substitute

(AO-Al-A2-Bl-B21-C4-D12-C5-E52-Fl-F31-F32-F20-F23-G72-G73-G82-G13-G2-G6-Il-J

31-J32-J33-J6-K62-K42-M31-L4-M22-M23-M5-N4-03-P2-Rl-Tl-T2-Z2, hereinafter

referred to as “Route CCG”) as the “best meets” route. Every chart, exhibit,

distance-band buffer, BLM/USFS handbook page, GIS layer, and Top-20 opposition

table is in service of that one move. Notably, Ms. Reinecke's testimony simultaneously

recommends a route using G6 and documents substantial public opposition to G6 in her

own Table RLSR-16. This contradiction is addressed in detail below.

Q. Based on your review and analysis of Ms. Reinecke’s testimony and the

Exhibits included with her testimony, did you identify any flaws or omissions in

her analysis that are relevant to the criteria required for Commission approval in

PURA § 37.056(c)(4); 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B)?


                                                        Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Ryan Hopkins​
                                       on Behalf of the G6 Landowners Legal Fund LLC regarding ​
                                                Reinecke Testimony for Cherokee Creek Partners
                                                                           PUC Docket No. 59475​
                                                                SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                    Page 10 of 29
 A. Yes, I did.

Q. What was the first flaw or omission that you identified in Ms. Reinecke’s

testimony?

A. The substitution of G6 for G51-G52 and N4 for N3 is not analyzed at the

individual-link level. The defense of Route CCG is made purely at the aggregated-route

level, on limited aggregated criteria she selected.

Ms. Reinecke’s testimony did not produce a Features Map for G2-G6; did not count

habitable structures along G2-G6; did not measure ROW parallelism on G2-G6; did not

perform a slope or stream-crossing inventory on G2-G6; did not perform a

Golden-cheeked Warbler-habitat overlap analysis on G2-G6; and did not perform a

foreground/middleground viewshed analysis on G2-G6.

The N4 substitution is completely unsupported and unjustified. N4 appears only inside

the link sequence in three citations. Ms. Reinecke includes in her testimony no written

justification, no supporting exhibit, no field count, and no viewshed analysis regarding

the insertion of the N4 link. She provides no Features Map; no habitable structures

count; no analysis of ROW parallelism; no slope or stream-crossing inventory;or any

FAA airfield-clearance review for the N4 link.

Q. Did you identify any flaw or omission in Ms. Reinecke’s testimony regarding

her consideration of engineering constraints?




                                                         Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Ryan Hopkins​
                                        on Behalf of the G6 Landowners Legal Fund LLC regarding ​
                                                 Reinecke Testimony for Cherokee Creek Partners
                                                                            PUC Docket No. 59475​
                                                                 SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                     Page 11 of 29
 A. Yes, 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B) requires consideration of engineering constraints and

cost. While Ms. Reinecke cites this requirement, she fails to perform an engineering or

cost analysis of CCP’s proposed routes. There is no analysis of length, cost per mile, or

premium as compared to Route 894. Using the Applicants’ own official cost data from

Interchange Filing No. 3787, Route CCG has an estimated total project cost of $2.150

billion, compared to the Route 894 cost of $2.076 billion, a cost premium of $74 million

over Route 894 that Ms. Reinecke's testimony does not acknowledge or justify.

Ms. Reinecke quotes, on page 8 of her testimony, the Commission’s definition of

prudent avoidance from § 25.101(a): “The limiting of exposures to electric and magnetic

fields that can be avoided with reasonable investments of money and effort.” However,

she failed to include in her testimony any analysis of electric and magnetic field

exposures along Route CCG, and failed to analyze the “reasonable investments of

money and effort” needed to deliver Route CCG.

Q. Did you identify any flaw or omission in Ms. Reinecke’s testimony regarding

habitable structures?

A. Yes. Route 894 has 85 habitable structures within 500 feet of the centerline and

ranks in Quartile 1, the best quartile, for habitable structures. Route CCG has 105

habitable structures and ranks in Quartile 2. This constitutes a 20-structure differential,

a 24% increase over Route 894. Ms. Reinecke dismisses that differential, at page 68,

line 12 of her testimony, on the ground that it “falls within one standard deviation” of the

dataset. There is no basis in the Commission’s rules for Ms. Reinecke’s conclusion that
                                                          Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Ryan Hopkins​
                                         on Behalf of the G6 Landowners Legal Fund LLC regarding ​
                                                  Reinecke Testimony for Cherokee Creek Partners
                                                                             PUC Docket No. 59475​
                                                                  SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                      Page 12 of 29
 a habitable-structure differential within one standard deviation is immaterial. A 24%

difference is significant and material and is a basis for the Commission’s decision to

reject Route CCG.

Further, Ms. Reinecke’s own aerial recount of Barn/Garage/Shed (“BGS”) structures,

beginning at page 68 of her testimony, supports a rejection of Route CCG. Her recount

shows Route 894 has 36 BGS and Route CCG has 57 BGS, a 21-structure differential.

Adding the habitable-structure differential of 20 to the BGS differential, Route CCG has

approximately 41 more structure-type identifications than Route 894.This difference is

again significant and material. Additionally, Ms. Reinecke’s own Table RLSR-13

documents that the number 1 public priority in both Question 5 (land use) and Question

7 (community resources) was minimizing impact on residential areas. (Reinecke

Testimony, at p. 74). Route CCG, with 41 more structure-type identifications, performs

worse on the public’s own stated top priority.

Q. Did you identify any flaw or omission in Ms. Reinecke’s testimony regarding

the visual-impact methodology she used for Texas private ranchland?

A. Yes, Parts 3–5 of her testimony are a wholesale reprint of the USFS Landscape

Aesthetics Handbook (~250 pp.). That handbook was developed for National Forest

System lands under NFMA, RPA, and NEPA. Neither PURA, the Commission’s rules,

nor any Commission order adopts the USFS Landscape Aesthetics Handbook as the

governing visual-impact methodology for Texas private ranchland.



                                                         Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Ryan Hopkins​
                                        on Behalf of the G6 Landowners Legal Fund LLC regarding ​
                                                 Reinecke Testimony for Cherokee Creek Partners
                                                                            PUC Docket No. 59475​
                                                                 SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                     Page 13 of 29
 None of the Bell County East-to-Big Hill corridor crosses National Forest System lands.

None of the corridor is on federal land at all. I am not aware of any prior Commission

CCN order that approved a route based on a USFS Landscape Aesthetics Handbook

viewshed methodology.

Ms. Reinecke’s testimony also referred to the Bureau of Land Management (“BLM”)

Visual Resources Inventory (“VRI”) Manual, which was included as Exhibit RLSR-6 to

her testimony. The BLM VRI Manual was developed for BLM-administered lands. None

of the corridor crosses BLM-administered land. Neither PURA, the Commission’s rules,

nor any Commission order adopts the BLM VRI Manual as the governing methodology

for transmission-line viewshed analysis on private Texas ranchland. I am not aware of

any prior Commission CCN order that approved a route based on a BLM VRI Manual

viewshed methodology on private Texas ranchland.

Q. Was there another flaw or omission that you identified in Ms. Reinecke’s

testimony?

A. Yes, Ms. Reinecke’s Table RLSR-16 (Part 1, p. 83) contradicts her G6

recommendation. G6 received 24 mentions on protest forms / opposition letters,

reflecting that at the time of her analysis the G6 link is the 16th most-opposed link by

protesters in the docket. Other links in Route CCG were also in the top 20 for most

protest forms/opposition letters: C4 (222 - Most opposed); D12 (105 - 6th most

opposed); C5 (95, 7th most opposed); G73 (59 - 9th most opposed). She “surmised

                                        on Behalf of the G6 Landowners Legal Fund LLC regarding ​
                                                 Reinecke Testimony for Cherokee Creek Partners
                                                                            PUC Docket No. 59475​
                                                                 SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                     Page 14 of 29
 [this result] to be directly related to population centers” but this conclusion is purely

speculative.

               AFFIRMATIVE ROUTE ANALYSIS AND RECOMMENDATION

Q. Have you conducted an affirmative route analysis to identify which routes best

meet the statutory criteria?

A. Yes. Because multiple witnesses filed direct testimony recommending G6-based

routes, specifically Route 572 (Brewer), Routes 295 and 296 (Brewer alternatives), and

Route CCG (Reinecke), I conducted an independent composite scoring analysis of 123

routes to identify which routes affirmatively best meet the statutory and regulatory

criteria of PURA §37.056(c)(4) and 16 TAC §25.101(b)(3)(B).

Q. What data did you use?

A. Every input in my analysis originates from the Applicants' own filed data: (1) Table

7-2 from Appendix E of the Environmental Assessment and Alternative Route Analysis

(Attachment 1), providing 33 quantified measurements for each of the 122 filed routes;

(2) cost estimates from Attachment 4; and (3) official Table 7-2 equivalent data provided

by the Applicants for alternative routes proposed by CCP, including Route CCG

(Interchange Filing No. 3787). I did not independently recalculate any of the Applicants'

environmental measurements.


Q. How did you construct your scoring methodology, and how did you assign

weights to each variable?
                                                          Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Ryan Hopkins​
                                         on Behalf of the G6 Landowners Legal Fund LLC regarding ​
                                                  Reinecke Testimony for Cherokee Creek Partners
                                                                             PUC Docket No. 59475​
                                                                  SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                      Page 15 of 29
 A. My methodology proceeds in three phases. First, I worked at the category level,

assigning a total point budget to each of the major statutory criteria categories,

reflecting their relative importance under PURA §37.056(c)(4) and 16 TAC

§25.101(b)(3)(B) and corroborated by the public input documented in Ms. Reinecke's

own Table RLSR-13. Second, within each category, I distributed the total category

weight across the constituent variables in proportion to their individual statutory

significance, environmental impact, and public priority. Third, I applied a normalized

percentile formula: each route's raw value is converted to a 0-to-1 scale relative to all

123 routes (0.0 = best, 1.0 = worst), multiplied by its assigned weight, summed, and

divided by the total weight to produce a composite score. Routes are ranked ascending:

the lowest composite score is the best-performing route.


The categories, their total weights, and the rationale for each are as follows:

           Category         Weight                       Statutory Basis & Rationale


 Habitable Structures         20     PURA §37.056(c)(4)(D) — prudent avoidance of residences. The

                                     single highest-weighted item in the entire model. Ms. Reinecke's

                                     own public engagement data (Table RLSR-13, Questions 5 and 7)

                                     confirmed that minimizing residential impact was the #1 community

                                     priority at every public meeting. The opposing expert's own survey

                                     validates this weight.


 Total Project Cost           20     PURA §37.056(c) — public interest and ratepayer protection. The

                                     Commission spends ratepayer funds; total project cost is the most

                                     comprehensive and legally correct cost metric. Note: Mr. Brewer

                                                  Reinecke Testimony for Cherokee Creek Partners
                                                                             PUC Docket No. 59475​
                                                                  SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                      Page 16 of 29
                                        cited only transmission line cost for Route 572 ($1.689B), not total

                                       project cost. Total project cost is the appropriate comparison.


Environmental Integrity         19.5   16 TAC §25.101(b)(3)(B)(iv); ESA federal nexus. Includes

                                       endangered/threatened species habitat (4 pts), riparian areas (3

                                       pts), open waters/lakes (3 pts), wetlands (2 pts), upland woodlands

                                       (2 pts), stream crossings (2 pts), stream paralleling (2 pts), irrigated

                                       cropland (1 pt), rare plants (1 pt), and cropland/pasture (0.5 pts

                                       each).


Engineering / Route             15     PURA §37.056(c)(4)(A); 16 TAC §25.101(b)(3)(B)(i)–(iii). Includes

Compatibility                          route length (4 pts), four parallel ROW types — existing

                                       transmission lines, railroads, highways, and pipelines (2 pts each)

                                       — and property boundary paralleling (3 pts). Compatible ROW

                                       scoring is inverted: more parallel mileage is better.


Historical & Aesthetic Values   10     PURA §37.056(c)(4)(C). Cultural resource sites crossed (4 pts),

                                       cultural resources within 1,000 feet (3 pts), and high archaeological

                                       potential areas (3 pts).


Community Values — Parks         9     PURA §37.056(c)(4)(B)–(C). Given the extraordinary level of

                                       community concern expressed in this record about parks and

                                       recreational areas, I treated parks as a separate elevated

                                       sub-category: parks traversed (4 pts), adjacent parks (3 pts), and

                                       foreground visual zone exposure (2 pts).


Community Values —              8.5    PURA §37.056(c)(4)(A); 16 TAC §25.101(b)(3)(B). Small airports

Aviation                               within 10,000 ft (3 pts); large airports within 20,000 ft (2.5 pts);

                                       private airstrips within 10,000 ft (2 pts); heliports within 5,000 ft (1

                                       pt).

                                              on Behalf of the G6 Landowners Legal Fund LLC regarding ​
                                                       Reinecke Testimony for Cherokee Creek Partners
                                                                                  PUC Docket No. 59475​
                                                                       SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                           Page 17 of 29
  Community Values —           4      PURA §37.056(c)(4)(A). FM/microwave installations within 2,000 ft

 Electronics                         (3 pts); commercial AM transmitters within 10,000 ft (1 pt).


 Community Values —           2      PURA §37.056(c)(4)(A). U.S./State highway crossings (1 pt);

 Infrastructure                      FM/county road crossings (1 pt).


 TOTAL                      109.5    33 variables; all weights disclosed; all scoring directions disclosed.




The opposing expert witness's own public engagement analysis, Reinecke Table

RLSR-13, independently corroborates the elevated weight assigned to habitable

structures and parks, the two highest-community-priority categories.


Q. What were the overall results of your composite scoring analysis?

A. The result that emerged from this analysis, built entirely from the Applicants' own

filed data, scored against the statutory criteria with fully disclosed weights developed

category by category from PURA and TAC, is that Route 894, the Applicants' own

proposed route, is Rank #1 of all 123 routes evaluated. I want to be clear about the

significance of this finding: I had no idea what route would rank highest when I began

this analysis, and I would not have predicted Route 894. The weights were developed

from the statute and the public record, independently of any knowledge of how they

would affect the rankings. The result is what the data produced when the correct

statutory priorities are applied correctly. A copy of the Excel document that reflects my

model, entitled RH_G6_Route_Rankings_Formula_Model, is attached hereto as Exhibit

A.

                                         on Behalf of the G6 Landowners Legal Fund LLC regarding ​
                                                  Reinecke Testimony for Cherokee Creek Partners

SECTION B — SCORING METHODOLOGY								
Step 1 — Min-max normalize each criterion across all 123 routes:								
Lower is Better:  norm(i,k) = [ MAX(k) – value(i,k) ] / [ MAX(k) – MIN(k) ]
Higher is Better: norm(i,k) = [ value(i,k) – MIN(k) ] / [ MAX(k) – MIN(k) ]
Result: norm ∈ [0,1]; 1.0 = best-performing route on that criterion.  If MAX=MIN, norm=1 for all routes.								
Step 2 — Weighted sum:								
WeightedScore(i) = SUM [ weight(k) × norm(i,k) ]  for k = 1…33
Maximum possible = Total Weight Pool (all criteria best). Weights are from 'Weights & Setup' sheet col D.								
Step 3 — Normalized score & rank:								
NormalizedScore(i) = WeightedScore(i) / TotalWeightPool
Rank = RANK(WeightedScore, all WeightedScores, descending).  All 122 application routes + Cherokee G ranked together.
